success_patterns: Every success was a one-step answer taken directly from the entity or word that recurs across the passages and matches the clue's distinctive anchors (title of the memoir, Greek 'leaf', Dec. 31 1999, Backbeat/Dorff, Gorky Park).

Where the clue had a pronoun or no 'this' pointer ('became the Duchess of it', 'It's the cry of a sheep or goat'), the agent still output only the missing entity: the bare place word 'York', or the dictionary headword 'bleat'. It did not echo the clue's words or give a definition.

The agent used the verb's direction or role to pick between two entities that both appear in the passages (the US relinquished control, Panama took control). It answered with the party that fits the verb.

The agent resolved 'actor played this <role>' clues by finding the passage line pairing actor and film with the real person ('Stuart Sutcliffe (Stephen Dorff)'). The clue's form hint 'alliterative' confirmed the full-name choice.
The agent completed a truncated J! Archive snippet (clue shown, answer cut off) using the entity that the other passages repeatedly tie to the clue's details.

patch.reasoning: Several successes depended on small, reusable checks that the skill states only partly or not at all. These are: checking verb direction when two parties appear, resolving pronoun ('of it') and bare-definition clues to the missing word or headword, treating 'played this <role>' as asking for the person or character portrayed, and treating form adjectives such as 'alliterative' as hard filters. Each edit is short and attaches to an existing section so it does not duplicate existing text.

edits.target: Do not choose one that fits only some.
edits.content: - Check the DIRECTION and ROLE of the clue's verb when the passages name two parties for the same event ('took control of', 'took over', 'acquired' vs 'handed over', 'relinquished', 'sold'). Answer the party that fits the verb: 'On Dec. 31, 1999 this country took control of the canal' -> 'Panama', not the US that gave it up.

edits.target: and answer with the common English name (Conch).
edits.content: - Pronoun-slot and bare-definition clues: in 'In 1986 Sarah Ferguson became the Duchess of it' the word 'it' is the blank. Answer only the missing word ('York'), not 'Duchess of York'. A clue with no 'this' that just defines something ('It's the cry of a sheep or goat') asks for the headword of the dictionary entries whose definition paraphrases the clue. Take the word that appears in the entry titles and glosses ('bleat'), not a clue word and not a synonym that fits only part of it ('baa').

edits.target: - Ask: what category is the answer (country, person, vitamin, object, band), and what member of that category fits all the clue details?
edits.content: - 'In <film/show> <actor> played this <descriptor>' asks for the real person or character portrayed, not the actor or the film. Find the passage line that pairs the actor with the role ('Stuart Sutcliffe (Stephen Dorff)') and give the name form the passages repeat. 'This <relation> of <famous person> who wrote <book>' asks for the author, so answer with the person the title is tied to.

edits.target: - Double-meaning clues ('Term for an international match, or what its players are "put to"', 'X, or Y'):
edits.content: (Form adjectives in the clue such as 'alliterative', 'rhyming', 'palindromic' or 'two-word' are hard filters on the answer, like a letter count. Test candidates against them: 'alliterative bassist' fits 'Stuart Sutcliffe' but not 'Stu Sutcliffe' or a nickname.)
